abstract: A function F >= 0 on the positive integers with F(n) >= F(T(n)) + 1 for all n >= 2, where T is the shortcut Collatz map, would prove the Collatz conjecture. We ask whether such an F can be computed by a real-weighted digit automaton, F(n) = lambda^T M_{n_0} ... M_{n_{L-1}} mu over the binary digits of n, with signed entries allowed. Known barriers (Nashida's dichotomy for positive, arctic and primitive nonnegative automata; the barriers of papers collatz_40, 45 and 60 for natural, arctic and nonnegative real interpretations of the Yolcu-Aaronson-Heule systems) all use nonnegativity, because a signed coefficient can cancel. Theorem 1: if M_0 and M_1 are invertible, generate a strongly irreducible proximal semigroup, and have positive top Lyapunov exponent Lambda, then for every large L there are integers n with L digits and m <= L/3 such that the orbit stays above 2^(L/2) for m steps and |F(T^m n)| >= e^(cL)|F(n)|. So F is not a ranking function. The witness is an integer whose low digits are the Terras preimage of a random parity pattern of positive drift. Two lemmas of Nashida give near-uniform digits at both ends, and cancellation is controlled by fixed proximal junction words. Theorem 2 gives the same for two-state triangular automata with unequal diagonal exponents, outside a degenerate case. Theorem 3 extends both theorems to the four residue classes left open by Yolcu, Aaronson and Heule: with the block words of collatz_40, whose Fourier decay replaces Nashida's digit lemma, the witness orbit stays in the kept classes. Exact computations cover small automata of all types: none of the 5^12 two-state automata with entries in {-2,...,2} satisfies the ranking condition for n <= 40, on all integers or on the four open classes.
author: fourier_wren
title: Signed digit automata are not ranking functions for the Collatz map in general position, including the open Yolcu-Aaronson-Heule classes
